articles.title: Callum Walsh: From working on fishing boats to ferocious sparring at the Wild Card gym - the making of a fighter
articles.summary: Callum Walsh doesn't back down from danger; he's gone from working on fishing boats to forging a stellar amateur career, proving himself at the famous Wild Card gym and insists he's ready for anybody in the sport; Walsh fights Tyler Denny on Saturday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
On Saturday, live on Sky Sports , he fights former European champion Tyler Denny at the 3Arena in Dublin.

It will be a test for Walsh against a dangerous opponent, one that he welcomes.

"I'm ready for anybody. I love to challenge myself. I love to fight," Walsh told Sky Sports .

The Irishman is returning to the 3Arena for his first fight in Dublin since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024.

"It was one of the best nights of my life. Walking out in front of that crowd was insane," the 25-year-old said. "It looks like there was 20,000 people there and it felt like there was 20,000 people there.

"It was crazy. I can't even describe it."

He's come a long way from working on fishing boats as a teenager in Cork. That was a demanding profession with its own kind of dangers.

"I got this fishing job just randomly, I didn't want to work anywhere inside," Walsh remembered.

"It was seven days a week, it was hard work, it wasn't easy but the best job ever in the summer, when it's sunny and you can jump off the boat and swim. You start at four o'clock in the morning. It was very hard [work].

He'd haul crab and lobster pots on deck, rebait them and send them back to pulled down by their anchor.

"If you stack them in the wrong order, you're [in trouble]. The whole boat is going to go. Crazy. It's dangerous work," Walsh explained.

"If they're in the wrong order you're going to have rope all over the place, there's going to be stuff flying. You're going to get tangled up, you're going to get dragged overboard, dragged down with them. Even if it's four or five o'clock in the morning you have to be switched on.

"[One time] I put them back in the wrong order, my leg got trapped on the side of the boat between the rope and the boat, but we were able to get the boat in reverse quick and I was able to get my leg out. Stuff like that is very dangerous if you don't know what you're doing."

All the while he was pursuing a highly decorated amateur career which saw him winning medals domestically and on the international scene.

But he chose to pursue professional boxing and found his way to Freddie Roach's famous Wild Card gym in LA. He had to prove himself straightaway. Roach threw the youngster into sparring on his first day.

"If you want to train here, you have to spar.' He [Roach] wanted to see if I was even worth being there. I sparred the first day and he told me to come back again tomorrow," Walsh said.

"I was in there sparring everybody and anyone for a year and then I made my pro debut.

"Someone will come in [to the Wild Card] for sparring, you know that they're not really supposed to be there," Walsh continued.

"Freddie would tell you: 'Show this guy he's not supposed to be here.' I've knocked so many people out in that gym, I've seen so many people not come back. That's how it is. Freddie Roach's gym is known for being one of the best gyms in the world, known for tough sparring and Freddie he takes pride in that."

His experiences in California helped forge the fighter Walsh is today. "Coming from a massive amateur background, to learning the pro style and how aggressive his pro style is. I think it's the perfect combination," Walsh said.

"Being able to go over to Freddie and learn that aggressive pro style from someone who's had so much experience, I think it's the perfect mixture"

He is determined to show what he can do against Denny on Saturday. "I just believe in my own ability. I just believe if I've trained and prepared to my best I can beat anybody."

articles.title: Joseph Parker says he will return to ring 'soon' after drugs ban lifted following failed test last October
articles.summary: Joseph Parker says he will be back in the ring 'soon'; traces of cocaine were discovered in a routine test given to the UK Anti-Doping Agency on the day of his defeat to Britain's Fabio Wardley in October
articles.body:
The heavyweight's routine test given to UK Anti-Doping on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley last October returned traces of cocaine following the loss by 11th-round stoppage at The O2.

Parker, who denied taking any banned substances, could have faced up to a two-year ban from boxing.

However, he has now released a statement saying his suspension has been lifted.

General Secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control, Robert Smith declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News but confirmed the suspension has been lifted.

"I'm pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I'll be back in the ring soon. I've been advised to say no more for now while details are finalised. Thank you to all my supporters," Parker said on Wednesday.

Parker, 34, is a former world champion who lost his belt to Anthony Joshua in 2018, but he went into his fight against Wardley in arguably the best form of his career.

After a punishing loss to Joe Joyce in 2022, Parker won his next six contests prior, picking up statement wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, as well as winning the WBO Interim strap.

He was due to challenge then-IBF belt-holder Daniel Dubois in February, only for Dubois to fall ill just days before the fight was meant to take place.

Parker put his position as the WBO mandatory challenger to undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk on the line by taking the fight against Wardley, but it was a gamble that backfired.

articles.title: Raven Chapman: Boxer undergoes emergency surgery after collapsing following sparring session in Denmark
articles.summary: Boxer Raven Chapman remains in hospital after collapsing following a sparring session in Denmark; she suffered a bleed on the brain and was rushed to hospital and underwent emergency surgery; Chapman fought Skye Nicolson for the WBC world featherweight title back in 2024
articles.body:
During training, Chapman collapsed and was rushed to hospital on July 24 where she was placed in a medically induced coma. A GoFundMe has been launched, with Chapman's team hoping she can return to the UK under medical supervision.

The statement from her management team read: "On Friday, July 24, Raven unexpectedly collapsed after a sparring session in Denmark. Emergency services were called immediately, and she was airlifted to a local hospital. She was diagnosed with a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

"Raven underwent emergency surgery immediately. The procedure successfully stopped the bleeding and helped stabilise the swelling. She was then placed in a medically induced coma. Over the past day, she has been taken off the sedatives and is continuing to receive treatment while awaiting medically supervised repatriation to a hospital in the UK, where her rehabilitation is expected to take some time.

"Her doctors are doing everything they can to support her recovery, and we remain hopeful as she continues to fight through this incredibly difficult time. Raven's family are in Denmark supporting her during this incredibly difficult time. We kindly ask that their privacy is respected.

"At this stage, this is the only update we are able to provide. If there are any significant developments, we will share further information when it is appropriate to do so. Thank you for your continued support. Please keep Raven and her loved ones in your thoughts during this challenging time."

Back in 2024, Chapman challenged Skye Nicolson for the WBC world featherweight title, with Nicolson winning by unanimous decision.

Nicolson commented on the post from Chapman's management with: "Praying for a speedy recovery. Can't believe this. Hearts broken for you champ. Keep fighting."

Founder of Queensberry Promotions Frank Warren, who used to manage Chapman, released a statement on social media on Wednesday, saying: "Raven is fully in my thoughts this morning, I'm really hoping she can pull through and get home safely.

"Everyone at Queensberry is behind you Raven, we're all hoping you can pull through this."

articles.title: Joseph Parker 'relieved' after drugs ban was lifted and could target winner of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley rematch
articles.summary: Joseph Parker denied taking any banned substances after returning traces of cocaine in a Voluntary Anti-Doping Agency test on day of defeat by Fabio Wardley in October; The British Boxing Board of Control confirmed the suspension has been lifted; Parker is set to fight again this year
articles.body:
The New Zealander returned traces of cocaine in a UK Anti-Doping test on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley in October, but Parker denied taking any banned substances and the British Boxing Board of Control confirmed the suspension has been lifted.

Parker's manager Higgins is planning the next career move for the former WBO world heavyweight champion, who could fight twice before the end of 2026.

"A combination of relieved, excited, and energised," said Higgins when asked about Parker's current mindset.

"Joseph is champing at the bit to get back into the ring. He was up early to go for a run this morning.

"He feels like he is at the peak of his powers and they say a heavyweight only reaches his prime in his thirties. Joseph is only 34 and if you look at the names on his resume, you could call him a veteran but he's still relatively young.

"Joseph has said to me that he would love to fight this year," Higgins added. "It could be a tune-up, then a big fight at the end of the year or it could be a big fight at the end of the year."

Parker has shared the ring with virtually every top heavyweight of his era, including Anthony Joshua, Deontay Wilder, Andy Ruiz Jr, Derek Chisora, Dillian Whyte, Fabio Wardley, Joe Joyce and Zhilei Zhang.

That 11th-round stoppage loss inflicted by Wardley stopped Parker's charge towards another world title, but Higgins is 'supremely confident' that the Kiwi can become champion again.

"Joseph is confident. He's done it before; he knows what to do. He's going to have another run at the title and is excited to do so.

"He's a free agent so right now we're looking at all offers. We'll look at anything that makes sense. We'll look at its merit on a risk-and-return basis.

"I'm supremely confident that he can become a world champion again. If you look at history, I think even Lennox Lewis copped a couple of losses and then in his 30s it all came together and he was unbeatable.

"We're not quitters and Joseph is looking forward to this final two or three run in his career."

Parker's old WBO belt lies in the hands of Daniel Dubois, who will defend it against Wardley in a rematch later this year.

A fight against the Dubois vs Wardley 2 winner is an option that excites Parker, who would also welcome a rematch with Dillian Whyte.

"If you recall, Joseph had a world title fight against Dubois scheduled and then he mysteriously pulled out a few days before the fight [through illness]," said Higgins.

"Bakole got slotted in; Joseph knocked out Bakole. But there is absolutely unfinished business there with both.

"Joseph is not afraid to get in the ring with anyone. He also has unfinished business with Dillian Whyte and we'd love that rematch.

"If the deal is right and the terms are right, he would love to make any of those fights happen."

articles.title: Jake Paul's rematch with Tommy Fury 'makes most sense' as American star plans boxing return, says Nakisa Bidarian
articles.summary: Jake Paul eyes return to boxing by January after sustaining broken jaw in Anthony Joshua loss; Tommy Fury rematch is possible comeback fight; watch Cherneka Johnson vs Dina Thorslund battle for undisputed world titles, live from 3am on Sky Sports this Sunday
articles.body:
Paul has not been seen in the ring since suffering a sixth-round defeat to Anthony Joshua in December 2025, during which he suffered a broken jaw in two places at the hands of the British heavyweight.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer has recovered, rehabilitated and set his sights on a comeback within the next five months.

"In terms of timing, we continue to focus on the end of this year or January. That's the timeline for his return," Bidarian, Paul's partner at MVP, told Sky Sports .

Paul's defeat to Joshua was the second of his 14-fight career, with the only other blemish on his record coming against Fury in 2023, a split decision points loss after the Brit had been floored in the final round.

Victories over former heavyweight world champion Mike Tyson, former middleweight world champion Julio Cesar Chavez Jr and ex-UFC star Nate Diaz have helped Paul earn credibility in the sport, and Bidarian now believes the time is right to avenge his defeat to Fury.

"If we're able to come to terms with Tommy, that's the fight that makes the most sense," he added. "If you think about where they were three years ago, it's the perfect opportunity to show the world that both of them have evolved as boxers.

"For Jake, coming off the loss to AJ, this is his chance to really demonstrate that he has moved to another level, and for Tommy this is his opportunity to say the Jake Paul story has come to an end."

Asked what obstacles stood between Paul and Fury signing a second fight, Bidarian replied: "Money, expectations and the reality of the economics."

Since the Paul victory, Fury has beaten YouTuber KSI on points and also defeated former World's Strongest Man Eddie Hall by majority decision in a Misfits Boxing exhibition bout in June.

articles.title: Joseph Parker: Former heavyweight champion claimed failed drug test was caused by cocaine use of nutritionist ahead of Fabio Wardley fight
articles.summary: Joseph Parker returned an adverse analytical finding for a metabolite of cocaine during a UKAD test shortly after his surprise defeat to Fabio Wardley in London last October; UKAD have revealed Parker claimed the result was caused by exposure to cocaine being used by his nutritionist
articles.body:
Parker returned an adverse analytical finding (AAF) for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, during a routine UKAD test shortly after his surprise defeat to Fabio Wardley in London on October 25 last year.

The New Zealander, who has throughout the saga denied taking any prohibited substance, announced on Wednesday that his suspension, which could have lasted as long as two years, had been lifted and that he would be "back in the ring soon".

On Thursday, UKAD officially confirmed Parker was free to resume his career as details of the case were shared, which included the 34-year-old's explanation for the adverse finding.

A UKAD statement said: "On 6 March 2026, Mr Parker provided UKAD with evidence claiming that the AAF was the result of his exposure to cocaine used by the nutritionist he had employed in preparation for the bout on 25 October 2025.

"The nutritionist stated that he was a regular user of cocaine and had used cocaine daily in the week leading up to the bout.

"Between 14 April 2026 and 3 June 2026, UKAD requested further information from Mr Parker in relation to his explanation for the AAF. Amongst other matters, Mr Parker stated that he had first worked with the same nutritionist in April 2023."

UKAD explained that a decision had been made to impose a three-month period of ineligibility, which it already considers served, because an independent scientific expert was satisfied that any ingestion of cocaine had occurred out of competition, and therefore in a context unrelated to sporting performance.

The statement said: "On 15 June 2026, UKAD received an independent scientific expert opinion from its instructed expert, which concluded that Mr Parker's ingestion of cocaine most likely took place out of competition (i.e. before 11:59pm on 24 October 2025).

"On 22 June 2026, UKAD confirmed to Mr Parker that in light of the opinion from its expert, it was satisfied that any ingestion of cocaine occurred out of competition and for that reason would have been in a context unrelated to sport performance.

"Consequently, UKAD lifted Mr Parker's Provisional Suspension on that date (allowing him to resume his participation in sport with immediate effect) and proposed a three-month period of Ineligibility (deemed served) by way of sanction for his Anti-Doping Rule Violation."

The scientific expert believed it possible that Parker's administration of cocaine "may have occurred" from contamination, but also said they could not exclude the possibility the finding had arisen "as the tail end of the administration of a larger pharmacologically active dose of cocaine."

With the UKAD report, the scientific expert said: "It is also my opinion that Mr Parker's administration of cocaine may have occurred orally from food contaminated with cocaine by his sports nutritionist who has admitted being a user of cocaine giving rise to the finding of benzoylecgonine in Mr Parker's urine Samples.

"I cannot exclude the possibility that the finding of benzoylecgonine has arisen as the tail end of the administration of a larger pharmacologically active dose of cocaine."

The result of Parker's bout against Wardley, which was an 11th-round stoppage victory for the Brit, becomes a defeat by disqualification, rather than knockout.

Parker lost his world title to Anthony Joshua in 2018, but went into his fight against Wardley in arguably the best form of his career.

After a punishing loss to Joe Joyce in 2022, Parker won his next six contests prior, picking up statement wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, as well as winning the WBO Interim strap.

He was due to challenge then-IBF belt-holder Daniel Dubois in February, only for Dubois to fall ill just days before the fight was meant to take place.

Parker put his position as the WBO mandatory challenger to undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk on the line by taking the fight against Wardley, but it was a gamble that backfired.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn expects British heavyweight fight to be finalised by end of August despite concerns over location
articles.summary: Eddie Hearn insists Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will be finalised by the end of August despite concerns over relocating the fight to New York; Hearn asserts that Joshua is keen to fight Fury on British soil
articles.body:
New York has emerged as the most likely venue for Fury vs Joshua, with Madison Square Garden poised to host the two British stars.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn insists he is yet to agree that the bout can be moved to the States, but still expects the fight to be finalised this month.

"At the end of August, there will be a press conference," Hearn told Sky Sports News.

"I'm not going to sit here and tell you there's no way the fight's happening in America because things can change.

"But I really feel strongly that this is something that should happen in the UK and we'll do all we can.

"We're up against it - it seems like everybody else has agreed but Anthony Joshua. He feels a little bit of responsibility to UK fight fans as well, and he's doing everything he can to give them what they want."

Discussion about a change of venue has led to speculation that the fight could be delayed, but Hearn remains optimistic that an in-shape Anthony Joshua will be ready to fight in November no matter the location.

"We're ready to go in November - so there's no reason for this fight to be delayed," Hearn added.

"We will try and make it as financially unviable as possible to do this fight in the US, so that hopefully they just turn around and say, 'okay, let's just do it in the UK'.

"Apparently, [New York] is the entertainment capital of the world. Who cares? It's two Brits and the biggest fight in the British boxing history. But I understand business."

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Can fast-tracked 21-year-old Briton make history on Saturday?
articles.summary: Can heavyweight Moses Itauma become world champion at 21 by beating Filip Hrgovic on Saturday or has the fast-tracked Briton arrived too soon?
articles.body:
British heavyweight Moses Itauma pulls out his phone and scrolls through his pictures.

He shows a meme featuring former Nigerian president Olusegun Obasanjo in traditional attire, standing with his hands on his hips and staring deadpan into the camera.

"This is how an African dad looks at you when you pursue a career that goes against his wishes and you turn out to be successful," a chuckling Itauma reads aloud to BBC Sport. "That is pretty much my dad."

Itauma was born in Slovakia to a Nigerian father and a Slovak mother before moving to Kent as a young child.

His parents originally wanted him to become a doctor or a lawyer. But once his older brother turned professional and the family recognised Itauma's exceptional natural talent, their stance softened.

"Don't worry about school. Just focus on your boxing," his mother eventually said.

That decision has paid off spectacularly.

At 21, Itauma steps into the ring against Filip Hrgovic on Saturday for the vacant IBF title with the chance to become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in history.

"There's a lot of expectations on my shoulders to carry the flag of British boxing. I just have to live up to it," Itauma says.

Victory against Croatia's Hrgovic would put Itauma on the path to becoming the next big name in British heavyweight boxing, with Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua inching closer to the end of their storied careers.

Fury, with his Netflix documentaries and larger-than-life personality, has always made himself the attraction. Itauma is more like Joshua - guarded and keeping the media at arm's length.

"What irritates me most is when people think you're public property," he says.

"What people don't know about me is that I don't actually want to be in the limelight. The way my career is going, I just have no choice."

Like Joshua, Itauma often appears uninterested in the theatrics of fight week. When Hrgovic interrupted during Thursday's news conference, Itauma calmly asked host Adam Smith for the next question.

There are similarities in their careers, too.

Joshua fought Charles Martin for the IBF title in his 16th pro bout, having boxed 34 rounds. Itauma arrives at his first world-title opportunity a fight sooner and with 31 rounds logged.

While Joshua had an Olympic gold medal and a deeper amateur background, victory for Itauma would make comparisons unavoidable - eclipsing Joshua to become the fastest British heavyweight to win a world title.

Itauma's trainer Ben Davison, who also worked with Joshua and Fury, believes he has the temperament to handle what comes next.

"Moses has already had that pressure for such a long time and I just think it's water off a duck's back."

Should Itauma have been given a title shot?

Boxing's best young prospects tend to be handled carefully and are given time to learn before dangerous tests arrive.

Itauma, however, has been fast-tracked to his world-title shot.

Francis Warren - son of Queensberry chief Frank - first noticed him as a teenager, sparring established professionals. Former British heavyweight champion Jeamie 'TKV' Tshikeva was there even earlier.

"Moses was a big 11 or 12-year-old, around 75 to 80kg, (11st 11lb to 12st 8lb) and sparred an adult of the same weight," TKV says. "He really showed up, put hands on this grown man, and I was shocked.

"The guy he sparred was around 25. Imagine going home and telling your wife you got beat up by a kid."

Itauma's progress has been marked by destructive stoppages over Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin. They may not be world-beaters, but the manner of those wins strengthened belief Itauma was destined for the top.

When Oleksandr Usyk vacated the IBF title and Frank Sanchez agreed to step aside, Itauma's fight with Hrgovic was elevated into a world-title contest.

Suddenly, the fast track looked, to some, like a shortcut.

Hrgovic - even before the IBF belt was on the line - claimed Itauma had been handed "everything on a plate". On social media, there was a similar feeling - perhaps a final eliminator would have been a more natural way to earn his shot.

Itauma, though, has little interest in proving himself to the doubters.

"It's a lose-lose situation for me because if I win, I've done what people expect, and if I lose, it's just like, I wasn't as good as what I thought," he says.

"I don't find happiness in trying to please other people's expectations."

Mike Tyson's mark as the youngest heavyweight champion in history - 20 years, four months and 22 days - remains boxing's ultimate holy grail.

While that record has passed, victory over Hrgovic would make Itauma the second-youngest heavyweight champion ever and boxing's youngest active world champion.

The Chatham heavyweight has never fought 12 rounds. He has never even sparred 12.

"Although I haven't gone 12 rounds and I haven't taken one on the chin, I don't think that's a characteristic you need to become a heavyweight champion," he says.

But what happens when his power does not end the fight? What happens when an opponent is still standing in round eight, still dangerous, still coming back?

TKV, who has sparred Joshua, Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley, has seen enough behind closed doors to believe Itauma can handle it.

"Moses works hard even though he hasn't had to face adversity in his fights or training," he says. "I've never seen him slack. He's fast, sharp, a good learner and I rarely see him get hit.

"I believe he can do the rounds, too. He has the potential to dominate the division for years."

There is no doubt within Itauma's camp that he belongs at this level. But all the outside questions over timing, merit and readiness will fade when the first bell sounds.

On Saturday, the prodigy has 12 rounds - if he needs them - to write his own chapter in heavyweight history.

articles.title: All The Reasons The Road to AEW All In 2026 Has Been Chaotic
articles.summary: Although this weekend's event looks tremendous, All Elite Wrestling's path back to Wembley Stadium in London has been turbulent.
articles.body:
Although this weekend's event looks tremendous, All Elite Wrestling's path back to Wembley Stadium in London has been turbulent.

In 2018, The Elite bet on themselves and changed the landscape of professional wrestling. On Sunday, AEW will host its fourth annual All In at the venue that transformed its proof of concept into the company's biggest show of the year.

This year's match card features the potential coronation of a hometown sensation and the latest clash in a rivalry that has been brewing since 2023. If that's not enough to pique your interest, The Young Bucks will face Christian Cage and Adam Copeland in a dream matchup.

There are plenty of surprises and high-profile bouts worthy of such a big stage. It's a fantastic card, but the weekly programming leading up to the festivities has left something to be desired.

A New Day For AEW Felt Inevitable...Until It Didn't

The go-home episode of Dynamite perfectly encapsulated how bewildering this build has been at times. We were left with more questions than answers regarding the direction of some of the biggest stars.

Swerve Strickland's status and placement on the card have been unclear for weeks. Nevertheless, he is a common foe for both the former and reigning trios champions, and their confrontation created online buzz for The New Day's AEW debut.

After all, he is outnumbered, and Ricochet quickly dismissed Strickland's chances of finding anyone on the roster who still trusts him. Aligning with his real-life friends, Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed, in their first post-WWE appearance would even the scales.

However, AEW hasn't hinted at this possibility for the last two weeks. Strickland took on Jack Perry in Wednesday night's main event, and there was no mention of it on commentary or a tease after the match.

The following day, Tony Khan announced the Trios Roulette Royale match, featuring seven teams and three surprise participants. Still, it's baffling that there was no setup for this on the company's flagship series.

Will Ospreay's Convoluted Journey to All In

Nevertheless, the weeks leading to All In: London haven't been a total bust. Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné have stolen the show every week in the most consistent storyline.

Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay kick-started their feud at Redemption, and their one-on-one segment on the following episode of Dynamite was a home run.

It was a much-needed shift that refocused The Aerial Assassin's quest to become world champion on their long-standing rivalry.

Ospreay's stint with The Death Riders was divisive, but AEW seemingly stuck the landing in time. So, it was puzzling to see him take another detour to deal with The Don Callis Family.

Ever since the English wrestler returned at Revolution, his route to Wembley and championship gold has been clear. The 33-year-old was the hottest star on the roster before he took time off to undergo neck surgery.

Ospreay undeniably lost some of his momentum under Jon Moxley's tutelage. It's also safe to say everyone underestimated how much fans wanted to see Omega as champion again. This has created uncertainty in a crowning moment most were eagerly anticipating in 2024.

Omega's unexplained absences may be another sign that The Best Bout Machine is still adjusting to life after suffering with diverticulitis. Callis gave Ospreay a villain of the week to dispatch in the meantime, but his inclusion further complicated a simple storyline.

In comparison, "Hangman" Adam Page's pathway from the men's Owen Hart Cup to All In: Texas last year was much more concise.

AEW's approach to long-term storytelling often caters to its audience, but Ospreay's story has taken some unnecessary twists and turns.

The Continental Challenge Cup Felt Unwarranted

The Continental Challenge Cup was also a cumbersome way to set up Moxley vs. Nigel McGuinness. Many of the matches were excellent, but the tournament took up so much TV time that could have been used more efficiently.

To that end, it's a shame that McGuinness didn't get to cut a promo and connect the dots between Mox and his most notable rival, Bryan Danielson. It would've been so easy to craft an angle around his desire to prove himself against the leader of The Death Riders.

Instead, AEW diluted the prestige surrounding the Continental Classic into a vehicle to determine Moxley's opponent. It hardly seemed worth it in the long run. Hopefully, the company will refine the concept next year.

Nonetheless, All In: London will likely exceed expectations because AEW consistently produces the best wrestling pay-per-views.

Many of our gripes about the weeks leading up to it will seem like a distant memory when The New Day and Strickland open the show and Ospreay raises the world title.

It has been a bizarre few weeks, but we believe this will be an auspicious event for AEW.

articles.title: MJF Sounds Off on the State of Pro Wrestling, Being a Fan, Andrade and More Ahead of All In
articles.summary: This Sunday, AEW will head to Wembley Stadium in London for the annual All In pay-per-view.
articles.body:
This Sunday, AEW will head to Wembley Stadium in London for the annual All In pay-per-view.

Most of the matches will have titles on the line, but one of the few that doesn't still has title implications, as the winner of the Casino Gauntlet will earn a shot at the AEW World Championship.

MJF is set to be one of the first two competitors to enter the gauntlet, and he will have to contend with his current rival, Andrade El Idolo, in the process.

We had a chance to speak to MJF ahead of the PPV to discuss his feud with El Idolo, why studying the past is important and more.

Bleacher Report: You're set to enter the Casino Gauntlet, and so is Andrade El Idolo. What is it about him that gets under your skin so much?

MJF: "What is it that gets under my skin? How much time do you have? I don't like the fact that he walks around acting like he's some sort of sex symbol. I'm far more attractive than him.

"I don't like that he claims to be the best wrestler. How is that possible when I'm the one who is the one true champion? I don't like the fact that he parades around with this national title, acting as if he is about to make this title more important than my title. That's never happening in a million years.

"I don't like the simple fact that he talks about, 'I'm the real Latino man.' Well, what's special about that? We've got plenty of Latinos in All Elite Wrestling. We've got some of the best luchadores in all of the world. But there's only one Big Hebrew.

"So I guess what I don't like about the guy is he's so pompous, and frankly, I don't know what for. He's accomplished a couple of big wins. Has he ever beaten me? No. Will he ever beat me? No. Will he ever be AEW world champion? No. And the fact that he is even in this match, to me, is laughable.

"This guy doesn't have a prayer of winning this thing. Here's exactly what's going to happen at All In. And I really, really hope everybody is paying close attention when I say this.

"I'm going to win the Casino Gauntlet contract in back-to-back years because that's what I do. I'm going to execute that contract and prove beyond a shadow of a doubt that neither Kenny Omega nor Will Ospreay were ever actually world champion.

"Only MJF has ever been world champion because Ospreay is a little cheat and got involved in my match with Kenny Omega at Beach Break, so the match should have been thrown out. This whole entire situation is preposterous, but I'm going to right all those wrongs on August 30."

BR: "You mentioned Omega and Ospreay. Do you have a preference for which one you would rather face for the title?"

MJF: "I couldn't give a s--t. I've beaten both of them, and I did it with an easy, easy, lax amount of effort. Hell, I've beaten Kenny Omega twice. I had Will Ospreay beat in the same building we're heading to on August 30, and then he cheated because Daniel Garcia got involved.

"Are you noticing a pattern here? The only time MJF loses is when somebody else sticks their s--tty little nose in my business."

BR: "Wembley Stadium has taken on a life of its own leading to the PPV. Do you like performing in big venues, or do you prefer the more intimate atmosphere of somewhere like the ECW Arena?"

MJF: "Frankly, I don't have a preference. Listen, I wrestled in front of one of the biggest crowds of all time. It was 82,000 people. I main-evented that match, and I won. That's a feeling Will Ospreay and Kenny Omega will never get to have.

"But what I will tell you is this: I'm not concerned with who is outside of the squared circle. The only thing I'm concerned with is who's in it. And the fact of the matter is, when this match starts, it's going to be me at No. 2, Andrade at No. 1, and I don't want other people to come into the match.

"I don't want this to become a clusterf--k. I want to get in and get out, and that's exactly what I'm going to do, and I don't give a s--t if there's 30,000, 40,000, 50,000 people. Doesn't make a difference to me.

"I'm winning, I'm hitting the pay window, and I'm leaving."

BR: "When you came into AEW, you were billed as this young prodigy who could go in the ring and was great on the mic. Now that you have been in the business for over 10 years, what is the biggest thing you've learned about yourself as a performer in that time?"

MJF: "I think the biggest thing I've learned about myself is to only trust myself. The only time I've ever really gone south in my career, which was, in my opinion, one time and for a very brief period of time, was when I trusted Adam Cole.

"I put my head and my heart on the line. I have not put my heart on the line since. My heart's on f--king vacation, okay. I don't know if it's ever coming back home. The reason I've gotten to the position I'm in, and I will say it proudly, is because I'm heartless.

"The only thing I'm concerned with is being world champion, which I am. The only thing I care about is becoming incredibly rich and leaving a legacy in this industry. And I've managed to do all three of those things at the very old, hunched-over age of 30.

"In all sincerity, I think one of the biggest issues that young people in the industry make is that a lot of guys are busy walking around trying to find veterans in the locker room. Here's the deal and the god's honest truth.

"Not all of them, but 99 percent of the veterans in the locker room, they don't have your best interest, they don't want you to beat them, they don't want you to be better at talking than them or better at wrestling than them. Because if you're better than they are, that's taking food off their plate.

"The only person you can trust in this industry is yourself. Now, if you're a young reader who has piss poor instincts, then I can't help you. You're better off being a follower. Trust me, there are plenty of followers in this industry, and they make good money being followers, just not MJF money.

"And that's fine. Not everybody is a lead. Some people are born to be backup dancers. Some people are born to be stars. That is truly what I've learned. The only person that I can trust and should trust is myself and my own instincts."

BR: "You're a student of the game and watch both old and new wrestling. Who are the people you think young wrestlers should be studying?"

MJF: "Honestly, they should study me. You know, I always harken back to the '80s because that is the best era in professional wrestling, in my opinion. I would also talk about territory wrestlers, and I'll tell you why.

"I'll give you one name: Gino Hernandez. He is somebody I have been studying a lot, and the cool thing about Gino is that he's a guy that not a lot of people know. So if you're able to take something from somebody that nobody's ever seen, it's going to feel original. What's old school is new school, right?

"Gino had so many interesting ways he would approach both matches and promos. Then you have other guys from that era. This is a manager, and he was a great manager in that era. A guy by the name of Gary Hart, and no, he was not part of The Hart Family, which is probably why he's not boring as s--t.

"Gary just had a very intense way of speaking and approaching talking on camera, and there are a lot of guys like that who have been lost not only because of time, not because of a great legacy. I could honestly go on and on and name random names.

"You know what's another fun one? When people think of Jimmy Garvin, I fear that they predominantly think of that failed tag run that he had in WCW when he had to pretend to be a Freebird even though he was assuredly not a Freebird.

"If you watch Jimmy Garvin in his heyday when he's got the hair all the way out and the gorgeous robes, and was walking around with a gorgeous girl and talking all this mess. I remember the first time I saw him and I was like, 'Whoa, where did this guy come from?' And he had a lot of stuff that I was able to implement as well.

"I guess my point is, if you're a young wrestler, the best thing you can be is a student of the game. "Playboy" Buddy Rose. That's another one lost to the annals of time.

"I think there are always names and people that the mass public don't know who were actually really quite good for a period of time that you can take a lot from."

BR: "What are your thoughts on the state of pro wrestling across the board right now?"

MJF: "I don't know if you can say it's not in a good place when in the history of pro wrestling, this is the most amount of money that's ever been made off of pro wrestling ever between TV deals and gates.

"I'm a 30-year-old man and I've already sold more million-dollar houses than most Hall of Famers. I think wrestling is in a really good place. Now, do I think that much like any sport or platform, there's a way that it can improve? Absolutely.

"Personally, I'm getting really sick of there's like a homogenized standard of what good is bell to bell, and I would love to see more styles. It's like cake batter ice cream. I had cake batter on an almost daily basis, over and over and over again.

"But eventually, because the flavor was so rich, I kind of got sick of it. And I yearned for the days of vanilla. I couldn't handle anymore. And I think that's happened with wrestling.

"It's a good thing to have options. If there's one thing I can critique pro wrestling for, while also stating the reason that my rise was so meteoric, is because I gave people that different flavor of ice cream they've been yearning for. So that's my take."

BR: "Do you ever get to watch wrestling just for enjoyment anymore?"

MJF: "Enjoyment is such an interesting word. I watch more professional wrestling than any professional wrestler that is professional wrestling today, a billion percent.

"I am watching everything. I'm an unwell person when it comes to that, but I wouldn't say I watch it for enjoyment. I watch it for a couple of things. Product knowledge. I watch it for what the next big thing is, what the next big idea is.

"Most importantly, I like to tape study people that I could potentially be wrestling down the line so I am prepared for them. I know their weaknesses and strengths. But I can say easily that I'm sitting down, and much like a wrestling fan would but in a very different way, I am watching Raw and SmackDown and TNA and MLW and MLP and New Japan and Stardom. And I'm also watching indies, and I'm watching AIW, AAW, Beyond Wrestling."

BR: "Is there anyone right now that you are a particular fan of watching?"

MJF: "I was just in a three-way with him, and I think he's got a lot to offer. Nick Wayne. I think Nick Wayne's really special, and he also understands this is an aesthetic business and he's gotten himself in really good shape in a short period of time. That's something I really respect.

"I don't like them, but I think both Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher are the guys I'm going to be wrestling in the main events of pay-per-views, probably for the next 10-15 years. Outside of that, I don't think he's a sleeper pick because he's a former singles champion in our company, but I think Mark Davis, to me, is my favorite big man right now in wrestling, for my taste.

"He is so good, and what I love about him most is that everything he does feels different to me, and it feels like something that harkens back to old, like a Stan Hansen or a [Bruiser] Brody. So yeah, I enjoy his work quite a lot."

BR: "You're the only world champion in AEW with his own custom belt, the Triple B. Has there ever been any contact with Burberry?"

MJF: "It's a double-edged sword. They're either beyond over-the-moon happy, or they're upset. I don't know if they think they should be getting a kickback. Frankly, sometimes I think I should be getting a kickback for making Burberry as cool as I made it feel. But there has not been a conversation yet with Burberry."

BR: "The way we always like to end an interview is having the wrestler review a movie. Is there something you have watched that you would want to talk about?"

MJF: "I really, and this is not a deep take, but I thought the new Spider-Man movie kicked ass. That's my take. I love action and I love action stuff, so I adore both the DC Universe and the Marvel Universe."

You can listen to the full interview in the video above, and you can see MJF competing in the Casino Gauntlet match this Sunday at AEW All In.

articles.title: Final Picks for Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay and Entire AEW All In 2026 Match Card
articles.summary: All Elite Wrestling returns to London's Wembley Stadium for its biggest pay-per-view of the year, All In.
articles.body:
All Elite Wrestling returns to London's Wembley Stadium for its biggest pay-per-view of the year, All In.

Sunday's card features some extraordinary matchups, headlined by Kenny Omega defending the AEW World Championship against Will Ospreay.

Who will emerge victorious from that match and the others on the packed card? Find out in this preview of the August 30 event.

AEW International Championship: Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kyle Fletcher vs. Kazuchika Okada

Three former allies in The Don Callis Family will square off Sunday in a match with plenty of potential to be the best of this year's All In.

Fletcher is among the brightest young stars in professional wrestling and someone whose skills place him among the best in-ring performers of the last two years. The same could be said of Takeshita, who has been part of some of the best bouts AEW has produced in that same span.

Then, there is Okada, who has a long history of performing at his best in the biggest matches and moments.

Take all three, with a tangled web of a story and the unpredictable element of Callis, and there is plenty to keep an eye on in London.

Any of the three can leave with the gold, but this feels like Fletcher's match to win. The Protostar retains the gold and moves on from his former teammates and their long-running rivalry.

Falls Count Anywhere for TNT Championship: Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight

This might be the toughest match to predict on the entire All In card.

Common sense suggests Allin avenges the betrayal by Knight and stands tall at one of the company's signature events. While that may be the eventual outcome, it is one that does a disservice to The Jet.

First, Allin does not benefit in any measurable way from beating Knight, other than to pay off a storyline with the babyface going over. He is a former world champion, has already worn the TNT title twice, and has stood victoriously on the All In stage.

A win for Knight would not only further validate him as one of the future cornerstones of AEW, but also enhance his TNT Championship reign.

A loss, even to a top-tier star like Allin, would hurt his momentum after months of Tony Khan and AEW attempting to establish him as one of the promotion's next big things.

Knight wins here, undoubtedly via nefarious means, and retains his title in a match that should do plenty to protect Allin from a booking perspective.

AEW Women's Tag Team Championship: Brawling Birds vs. Divine Dominion

Divine Dominion's Lena Kross and Megan Bayne have dominated the competition since capturing the AEW Women's Tag Team Championship from Willow Nightingale and Harley Cameron in March, but their five-month reign runs out Sunday.

The Brawling Birds' Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter return home to England and do the unthinkable by defeating the seemingly insurmountable tandem to capture the gold in a defining moment in both women's careers.

Expect a hard-hitting war that ends with the challengers finally overcoming Bayne and Kross to take the titles in the first big, fan-service moment of what figures to be many.

Prediction: Brawling Birds win the titles

Casino Gauntlet Match to Determine No. 1 Contender to AEW World Championship

Announced in advance of Sunday's big multi-man match to determine the top challenger for the most coveted prize in the company are Andrade El Idolo and MJF, with strong indications that Tommaso Ciampa and Chris Jericho will also enter the contest.

The match has been the setting of more than one memorable AEW debut over the years and, while that may be the case again as the company pulls out all stops to make the London show feel like a spectacle, this one should center on El Idolo and The Salt of the Earth.

El Idolo and MJF have been entwined in an escalating rivalry for months, with the former's betrayal of the heel at Forbidden Door being the difference in the heel team's loss to Team Briscoe in the Death's Door steel cage match.

Their rivalry is at the center of the contest, and while El Idolo has become a legitimate success story in his second run with the company, this is MJF's match to win.

The story of the world title picture in AEW in 2026 has been all about MJF. Sure, Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay headline Sunday's show and Darby Allin had a stint as champion, but it is MJF who has best filled the role of Triple H circa 2000 as the centerpiece heel who always finds himself in the mix, regardless of which wrestler has his attention.

MJF wins here to earn a future title shot at the winner of Sunday's main event, and inevitably he ends the year holding the gold.

AEW Continental Challenge Cup Final: Nigel McGuinness vs. Jon Moxley

In a perfect world, McGuinness would pay off his run through the Continental Classic tournament with an inspiring victory in front of his friends and family in London.

That may still happen, especially at a show in which the company tends to deliver happy endings.

Unfortunately, it seems rather unlikely that McGuinness beats the company's measuring stick, Moxley, for the AEW Continental Championship.

Unless the goal is for McGuinness to lose it in short order in an attempt to put over a heel, it would seem like the most logical outcome is a match in which the Londoner shows the toughness that he has throughout his storied career before succumbing to the reigning champion.

A show of respect after the contest should ease the fans' dissatisfaction over the finish.

Prediction: Moxley wins the tournament, retains the title

AEW World Tag Team Championship: Adam Copeland and Christian Cage vs. Young Bucks

Two of the most influential teams of the last 25 years square off in London as Copeland and Cage defend the AEW World Tag Team Championship against The Young Bucks.

A dream match for fans of tag team wrestling, it should have a red-hot crowd behind it as the prospects of the two teams battling again are relatively low, with age and story dictating this could be their sole meeting.

Copeland and Cage captured the gold from FTR at Double or Nothing on May 24. The challengers earned this title opportunity by teaming with The Rated R Superstar to defeat The Don Callis Family.

Though the story could have been a bit better for a match of this magnitude, the athletes involved and their rich history in the industry sells itself.

The Bucks winning would be a big moment, especially on this stage, but it feels a bit early in the champions' reign to switch the titles, especially with another notable dream match potentially waiting.

AEW Women's Championship: Willow Nightingale vs. Mercedes Moné

Mercedes Moné won the 2026 Owen Hart Foundation Women's Tournament to earn a shot at the AEW Women's World Championship, setting up a showdown with old rival Willow Nightingale that has produced some of the best TV of this build to All In.

Nightingale proving to be the obstacle Moné cannot hurdle to win the title that has eluded her to this point in her AEW run would have been an intriguing story and one that the company easily could have told with a successful title defense by the babyface in London.

However, Tony Khan confirmed during a media call ahead of All In that Nightingale is suffering from a legitimately broken hand (h/t Fightful ). She still plans on competing but depending on how long the recovery time is, it would certainly appear as though that outcome is no longer on the table.

It may never have been, either, with Moné's comeback and victory in the aforementioned tournament seemingly pointing toward the triumphant moment at AEW's signature event.

Participants: Hangman Adam Page and Brodido (champions), The Death Riders, The Dogs, The Bang Bang Gang, The Demand, and a Mystery Team

AEW World Trios champions "Hangman" Adam Page, Bandido and Brody King will defend their titles in a Trios Roulette Royale match, with some incredibly tough competition.

There is a mystery team yet to be revealed and, considering Swerve Strickland's confrontation with the champions in Las Vegas on Dynamite, one would have to assume he would be part of that threesome. Who would be his partners, though?

Who? Could it be a New Day in AEW? Perhaps.

If it is and the duo of Austin Creed and Kofi Kingston make their debuts alongside Swerve Strickland, they are the obvious winners. If not, a successful title defense is in order.

AEW World Championship: Will Ospreay vs. Kenny Omega

The build to Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship has been lacking, but there is more than enough established history between the two to get fans excited about the rare matchup.

Omega holds two victories over Ospreay in their three contests, with the lone loss coming after The Aerial Assassin, then a heel with The Don Callis Family, used a screwdriver on his forehead and finished him with a career-threatening Tiger Driver 91.

The champion has claimed that victory is without merit thanks to the circumstances, setting Ospreay up to prove he can beat The Best Bout Machine in his hometown of London and with the top prize in the company on the line.

It is a big-money matchup between two wrestlers synonymous with "best in the business" conversations over the last decade and a contest befitting the moment.

While there is a possibility that AEW and Tony Khan could swerve the wrestling world with a stunning outcome, this feels like the biggest foregone conclusion of any on the card.

Ospreay heads to the top of the company in a career-defining moment.

articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: Amanda Serrano fight changed my career but I'm even better now, says Reina Tellez
articles.summary: Texan contender Reina Tellez fights Jessica Barry on the undercard of Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron's main event in Birmingham this Saturday, carrying the lessons of her clash with boxing icon Amanda Serrano earlier this year; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 23-year-old made a name for herself back in January when she agreed to fight seven-division champion Amanda Serrano on just 15 days' notice, going the distance in a points defeat to the Puerto Rican icon.

Now Tellez, hailed as a 'warrior' by Serrano for her performance, is preparing to face Jessica Barry on the undercard of Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron's main event at MVPW-06 in Birmingham this Saturday.

"I believe in myself and I have a lot of heart. This is something I've always wanted to do, ever since I was a child," Tellez told Sky Sports .

"Having somebody that I watched growing up (Serrano) and then having the opportunity to fight her, it meant so much to me. And to make my family proud and to prove something to myself. So I took it considering the short time.

"I had a great outcome, even though it wasn't a win. I got a lot of things from that fight. Like I said, I'm grateful."

Tellez, who is 13-1-1 (5 KOs) as a professional, had previously been scheduled to face Juliana Vanesa Basualdo on the Stephanie Han vs Holly Holm 2 card in May, however the fight did not go ahead.

She now features on a landmark bill as MVP celebrate their fifth anniversary this weekend, Tellez crediting her decision to fight Serrano at last-minute notice as a catalyst for her latest opportunity to shine.

"The Serrano fight got me on a platform like I am today. For that, I'm extremely grateful," she continued.

"I feel like without that fight, I wouldn't be able to see the things that I need in my life and in my career to keep being successful and keep being Reina. It taught me a lot as a boxer and as a person.

"It means a lot to me. I'm not the same fighter that I was when I fought Amanda Serrano, and even my fights before that, I feel like I've really evolved.

"So to see how much better I've got over the past couple of months and the changes that I've made that I can showcase in the ring, it means a lot to me. This fight means so much to me, my family and my team. So I'm grateful for it."

Serrano recently clinched the 50th win of her professional career with a majority decision victory over Lucrecia Manzur to retain her WBA and WBO featherweight titles.

The fight had been broadcast live on TikTok and drew a total of 3.4m views across the night.

"You look at everything she (Serrano) has done, she's done a lot for the sport," said Tellez. "She's a world champion for a reason. So you have to always give respect to her too."

Tellez fell into boxing as a child growing up in Vero Beach, Florida having regularly watched the sport on television while also seeing her uncle train at the local gym. It would later prompt her to relocate in order to further her career inside the ring.

"I told them I wanted to box, and at first they didn't want to because I'm the only girl in the family," she said.

"And then they took their chance on it, they took me to the gym and since then I've just been boxing."

These days she operates out of San Antonio, Texas as one of two fighters alongside Miranda Reyes to represent a state boasting its fair share of boxing greats this weekend.

"Texas is big, boxing is huge in Texas, that's one of the main reasons I actually moved to Texas," she continued.

"It's just crazy to see people that I've known since even as a kid be here. And I'm happy for everybody who comes from where I come from to be able to get the opportunity. So best of luck to Miranda and to me."

articles.title: Chungreng Koren falls to Ryo Tajima in Road to UFC semifinal
articles.summary: MMA News: NEW DELHI: Chungreng Koren’s Road to UFC Season 5 campaign came to an end on Friday as the Indian fighter suffered a unanimous decision loss to Japan’.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chungreng Koren’s Road to UFC Season 5 campaign came to an end on Friday as the Indian fighter suffered a unanimous decision loss to Japan’s Ryo Tajima in their bantamweight semifinal in Shanghai.Koren, who had entered the semifinal after submitting Japan’s previously unbeaten Ryuho Miyaguchi in the quarterfinals, was unable to turn his grappling control into enough effective offence throughout the 15-minute contest.The Indian started aggressively, using leg kicks before taking the fight towards the cage. Koren eventually secured a takedown and looked to establish control.Tajima, however, quickly worked his way back to his feet and briefly managed to take Koren’s back.In the second round, even though Koren repeatedly looked to put Tajima against the cage, the Japanese continued to find opportunities to score with short punches. He also connected with a right hand during the round.Koren continued to press forward in the third round and again took Tajima down. He spent long stretches controlling the Japanese fighter on the mat and finished the contest with more than eight minutes of control time.Tajima, though, continued to work whenever he found an opening. He landed short punches and knees during the exchanges, and those moments ultimately proved important as the fight went to the judges.The scorecards were 30-27, 29-28 and 29-28, all in favour of Tajima.The defeat ends Koren’s run in the tournament and leaves him short of the Road to UFC final, where a tournament victory would have earned a UFC contract.The loss also brings an end to what had been a significant second chance for the Manipuri fighter.Koren had entered the tournament’s opening round in May on short notice after initially being named as a backup. He had struggled to make the bantamweight limit before facing Miyaguchi in Macau but produced an impressive comeback inside the cage, dropping his opponent with a left hand before securing a rear-naked choke in the second round.Ahead of the semifinal, Koren had spoken about how different his preparation was this time. He had spent three months at home, returned to training after a short break and also worked in Phuket with UFC fighters and other high-level training partners.The 27-year-old had also spoken openly about the difficult period that followed his loss to Rabindra Dhant in 2025. That defeat had left him struggling with his discipline and physical condition, forcing him to rebuild his routine before getting another opportunity on the Road to UFC.This time, he made weight and entered the fight with a full camp behind him.But Tajima proved difficult to break down.For Koren, the result means another UFC opportunity has slipped away. articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron expert predictions: Who wins super-welterweight title fight at MVPW-06 in Birmingham?
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron fight for the WBO, WBA and WBC super-welterweight world titles in the main event, with Caroline Dubois in action against Amelia Moore in Birmingham; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports from 7pn Saturday
articles.body:
Alycia Baumgardner (WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion):

"It's a great fight. I think they're both well skilled. But I think Mayer just edges it just a tad more than Cameron just because of her adversity that she went through. I think specifically because of me, too. You think about that loss.

"I've thought about the loss, and you want to revenge it somehow. Mikaela's done a great job. She's gone on. She took the L, she moved on, and she's done great for herself. I think that this fight will solidify her career just in making the big fights possible. I think that's just what she has in her career. I credit her."

Ellie Scotney (former undisputed super-bantamweight champion):

"I feel like stylistically it's a fight that you can get someone to watch boxing and they'll love boxing after watching it, I think it's going to be non-stop. I think it's going to be a fight for the ages.

"I think the winner of it breaks out, of course they're in the pound for pound list, but I think they'll be mentioned in the top four greatest fighters of all time within female boxing. They both love to fight, and I think for that factor they're going to give you everything.

Johnny Nelson (former cruiserweight champion):

"Even though I'd like to say Chantelle Cameron, I think Mikaela Mayer has a little bit too much variety, experience inside and outside the ropes. I would lean towards Mikaela to beat Chantelle on points even though it will be a fascinating fight. She has the height, the reach, the variety in her style of fighting."

Reina Tellez (American featherweight contender):

"I'm team Mayer. She's a great person and an amazing athlete. Chantelle is also an amazing athlete. You know, clearly she's a world champion for a reason, and she's had a lot of amazing fights. You've got to give the respect where it's due. I take nothing away from Chantelle, but I think Mayer might edge this one out.

Caroline Dubois (WBC and WBO lightweight world champion):

"It's a great fight, a great matchup, I think it will be action packed, they both come to fight. I think I'm going to go on the fence. I have a lot of love and respect for both women, at the end of the day I think boxing wins and I want to see both of them do well."

"I think it's a very close fight. I wish it was three minute rounds. I think it's going to be non-stop action. Chantelle Cameron, I've said it time and time again, if Katie Taylor is one of the goats, Chantelle Cameron is one of the goats of women's boxing.

"She went to Ireland, hostile territory, beat Katie Taylor, went back and almost beat her again in a close decision. And Mikaela Mayer, if she beats Chantelle Cameron, then she's one of the goats. So it's a goat versus a soon-to-be goat if she wins. Chantelle cements her legacy as the goat if she dominates Mikaela Mayer. I think it's very hard to predict, very, very hard to predict.

"What I can predict, nonstop action that is going to have you at the edge of your seat every single second of every minute of every round."

Amelia Moore (American lightweight contender):

"Chantelle is incredible, she has great pressure, IQ. Mikaela has distance, a really good distance control. And I have talked to people before about this. It's really going to be reliant on distance control and pacing. I really believe that. So it's who can maintain that pacing and be able to handle that distance control who is going to take it. I can't give you a prediction."

Mikaela Mayer (WBA and WBC super-welterweight champion):

"It pans out leaving Chantelle Cameron fans just flabbergasted. Just like, oh, s***, we lost all of our money. I can't believe Mikaela boxed that well."

Chantelle Cameron (WBO super-welterweight champion):

"I beat her by turning up, being me, doing what I do best and relaxing."

articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron split by security after clashing at fiery weigh-in
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron fight for the WBO, WBA and WBC super-welterweight world titles in the main event, with Caroline Dubois in action against Amelia Moore in Birmingham; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports from 7pn Saturday
articles.body:
The two rivals locked foreheads in the middle of the stage before trading insults as a fired-up Cameron vowed to "smash her head in" ahead of Saturday's blockbuster super-welterweight world title fight in Birmingham.

American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs), the WBA and WBC belt-holder, came in at 148lbs and three pounds lighter than her last fight against Mary Spencer back in October 2025.

WBO champion Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) followed in at 147.6lbs for what will mark her second contest at super-welterweight after April's victory over Michaela Kotaskova.

It beckons as one of the most high-profile fights in women's boxing, Mayer having reigned as a three-weight world champion and two-weight world champion Cameron the only woman to beat Katie Taylor in the Irish icon's professional career.

Rarely has either fighter flirted with the prospect of trash-talk throughout a respectful build-up to this weekend's main event, the two instead pointing towards their respective achievements and the ease at which they agreed to make one of the biggest fights in boxing.

The altercation appeared to be sparked by words exchanged between the pair upon making contact, Cameron seemingly unhappy with comments made by Mayer.

"She isn't intimating me, all that yapping, getting in my face, watch now, watch tomorrow," said Cameron.

"You're deluded. Shut your mouth, you are so deluded. I didn't say a word, you are making things up because you don't believe in yourself. You're going to get humbled.

"I'm gonna smash her f****** head in now."

Nobody saw this coming. Perhaps not even Mayer.

"She said I'm too slow, but there is no way Chantelle Cameron is faster than me," said the American.

"I didn't know this Chantelle Cameron existed, I like it."

Tensions also threatened to boil over once more between Caroline Dubois and Amelia Moore as the rivals delivered yet another volley of insults in their latest animated face-off.

WBC and WBO lightweight world champion Dubois tipped the scales at 134.8lbs before issuing a final warning to her American opponent.

"She knows I'm coming to take her head off. Welcome to my world," warned Dubois.

Moore hit back, insisting: "This is my world. I've been waiting my whole life for this point, my whole life."

The American challenger, who is 4-0 as a professional, was marginally lighter than her opponent at 134.4lbs.

Dubois could yet find herself on a collision course to fight WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion Alycia Baumgardner, who is stepping into the Londoner's division to face Elif Nur Turhan on November 8.

Elsewhere on the card Terri Harper came in at 137.8lbs as she returns to the ring for the first time since her defeat to Dubois in April.

She takes on another former opponent of Dubois in Houston's Miranda Reyes, who weighed in at 136.6lbs.

Coventry's Jessica Barry came in at 125.6lbs ahead of her clash with America's Reina Tellez, who weighed in at 125.6lbs having famously stepped in to fight Amanda Serrano at 15 days' notice earlier this year.

Tysie Gallagher (121.6lbs) is meanwhile preparing to make her debut under the MVP banner as she takes on Chicago's Brandi Robinson (121.6lbs).

articles.title: Moses Itauma vs Filip Hrgovic: Weigh-in turns heated with push and slap after final face off for IBF heavyweight world title fight
articles.summary: Moses Itauma receives slap to the face after pushing Filip Hrgovic off weigh-in stage following tense final face-off; both fighters weigh in lighter than their previous fights; Itauma, 21, is aiming to become Britain's youngest heavyweight world champion on Saturday at the O2 Arena
articles.body:
After taking to the scales - both fighters weighing in lighter than their previous respective bouts, with Itauma at 241.7lbs and Hrgovic at 236.2lbs - the boxers went face to face and were soon trading barbs.

As Hrgovic then moved to the front of the stage to flex for the crowd, Itauma pushed him in the back and the Croatian stumbled forwards and off the podium, keeping his feet.

Hrgovic then got back on stage and threw a slap at his British opponent's face as security stepped in.

Hrgovic told DAZN : "I just tell him what's going to happen, I'll smash him.

"He pushed me first so I just give him back, you know. He started. [The fight is] going to be tough."

Asked about the extra tension between them and why he had reacted the way he did, Itauma said: "I don't know, I just lost it a little bit. But we're here now, we're here. Let's go.

"I had a little itch and I just had to scratch it."

Itauma is aiming to become Britain's youngest heavyweight world champion and the second-youngest in history behind Mike Tyson by winning Saturday's fight for the vacant IBF heavyweight title at London's O2 Arena.

The undefeated 21-year-old has swept aside all those placed in front of him throughout his 14-fight career and stands on the brink of a historic victory that could shape the heavyweight division for a generation.

Tyson dethroned Trevor Berbick to seize the WBC belt at the age of 20 four decades ago.

Speaking ahead of the weigh-in about comparisons to Tyson's achievement, Itauma said: "I've always wanted to start off like Mike Tyson but [not] end up how Mike Tyson ended up.

"But now I'm in the shoes that Mike Tyson was, as in all the fame and accolades at such a young age, I'm starting to see and realise why he fell off the way he did. I just don't want to make the same mistakes he made.

"I'm wrapping my head around these things and I guess that's why I'm so heavily into books because I ain't never been in this position before.

"There is such thing as too early, but I'm taking necessary precautions to handle it the way I believe I should."

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Briton shoves opponent off stage, who responds with a slap
articles.summary: British heavyweight Moses Itauma pushes Filip Hrgovic off the stage before the Croat slaps him as chaos erupts at the weigh-in for Saturday's world-title bout.
articles.body:
British heavyweight Moses Itauma pushed Filip Hrgovic off the stage before the Croat slapped him as chaos erupted at the weigh-in for Saturday's world-title bout.

The pair will fight for the vacant IBF heavyweight title at London's O2 Arena, with Itauma bidding to become the second-youngest heavyweight champion in history.

The 21-year-old had refused to engage with Hrgovic's attempts to rile him during fight week but was in a fierce mood as the pair exchanged expletives during a charged face-off.

As Hrgovic turned to pose for photographs, Itauma shoved him in the back, sending the 34-year-old off the stage.

Hrgovic climbed back up, reached through security and slapped the Chatham fighter in the face before members of both teams became involved as security separated them.

"He pushed me first so I just gave it back. He started it," Hrgovic said, before breaking off from the interview to stare down Itauma.

Will fast-tracked Itauma become world champion at 21?

I'll send Itauma back to high school - Hrgovic

Itauma 'million times better' than Fury and Joshua - Hamed

Earlier in the week, Itauma said Hrgovic - who has repeatedly labelled him a "kid" - was beginning to get under his skin.

"I don't know, I just lost it a little bit. I had a little itch and I had to scratch it," Itauma said.

Before the fracas, an in-shape Hrgovic had weighed in at his lightest in seven years - 16st 12lb (107kg), 12 pounds lighter than for his victory over Dave Allen in May.

Itauma, who would also become the second-youngest world champion from Britain if he wins, weighed 17st 4lb (110kg), the same as for his victory over Jermaine Franklin in March.

Friday's ceremonial weigh-in took place at London's Spitalfields Market, with the official weigh-in held behind closed doors earlier in the day.

Several hundred people gathered around the food stalls and coffee kiosks for the event, with Itauma walking through the crowd to loud cheers.

He was smiling as he made his way through the market, where some had come specifically for the weigh-in while others were simply passing through and stopped to see what the fuss was about.

Itauma has the unbeaten record, knockout power and reputation as one of boxing's brightest young talents, but is still building his profile outside the sport.

Sometimes, though, it is what happens outside the ring that gets people talking.

The incident did not appear premeditated, with Itauma looking irritated by what Hrgovic was saying before the shove.

"He wants to stamp his authority and I think that's what he was doing there - stamping his authority before he gets in the ring," promoter Frank Warren said.

"He's showing he's not fazed by what Filip brings with his experience and sterling amateur background. He's up for this, alight and on fire."

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron butt heads at final face-off
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron butt heads in their final face-off before Saturday's light-middleweight unification bout in Birmingham.
articles.body:
Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron butted heads in their final face-off before Saturday's light-middleweight unification bout in Birmingham.

WBA and WBC champion Mayer and Briton Cameron had been cordial during the build-up but tensions spilled over at Friday's weigh-in.

As the pair came together to face-off at BP Pulse Arena, Cameron pushed her head into Mayer's and the American held her ground, pushing back before they ended up side-by-side and exchanging verbal insults.

"She isn't intimidating me," Cameron said after security stepped in. "All that yapping and getting in my face - just watch tomorrow."

Mayer, 36, claimed Cameron, 35, had said she would be "too slow", something the WBO champion dismissed.

"That's in your head, you're deluded. Shut your mouth, you're so deluded and you're making things up because you don't believe in yourself," Cameron responded.

After being pulled apart for a second time, Mayer added: "I didn't know this Cameron existed, she's going to need it."

Mayer and Cameron both came in 6lb shy of the light-middleweight limit at 10st 8lb (67kg).

Former undisputed light-welterweight champion Cameron has won 22 of her 23 fights as a professional, with her only defeat coming in a rematch with Katie Taylor in 2023.

Mayer is a three-weight world champion with 22 victories from 24 contests - losing to Briton Natasha Jonas and fellow American Alycia Baumgardner.

'Welcome to my world' - Dubois warns Moore

There was also plenty of tension when WBC and WBO lightweight champion Caroline Dubois and Amelia Moore faced off before their co-main event bout.

Dubois rolled her eyes and laughed during Thursday's news conference when Moore, who has only fought four times as a professional, said she had the tools to hand a first defeat to the Briton.

Both smiled as they were nose-to-nose on Friday with Dubois making her intentions clear as the weigh-in host placed a microphone between them.

"I told her I'm coming to take her head off," Dubois said.

Despite lacking experience in the professional ranks, 36-year-old Moore enjoyed a long amateur career and went through three Olympic cycles with the USA.

"It's very generic, she is saying the same thing to me that she's says to everyone," Moore said.

"It's a fight, Caroline. Welcome to the game. This is my world, I've been here a long time."

Moore tipped the scales at 9st 8lb (61kg) with Dubois one pound heavier as she looks to extend her unbeaten record to 15, having won 13 and drawn one.

articles.title: VICE's ‘Dark Side of the Cage’ dives into ‘Mayhem’ Miller’s long, troubled past
articles.summary: A new season of "Dark Side of the Cage" premieres Tuesday on VICE TV, and it features a look at Jason "Mayhem" Miller.
articles.body:
The second season of the acclaimed VICE Studios series "Dark Side of the Cage" premieres next week, and the opening episode is filled with mayhem – literally.

The season premiere goes inside the career of Jason Miller, whose "Mayhem" nicknamed proved to be prophetic when it came to not just his in-cage personality, but his outside-the-cage issues – which were plentiful for more than a decade.

The episode looks at the rise and eventual fall of Miller, who went from a youth struggling at home to a fighter who eventually became one of the first to cross over to the spotlight beyond MMA when he became the host of "Bully Beatdown" for three seasons on MTV.

Key look-backs in the episode include his training camp for Michael Bisping after they coached Season 14 of "The Ultimate Fighter" opposite each other – and his first arrest not long before the fight. On-hand to recall the incident are Miller's parents and sister – who was the one who called the police on him and leaked the story of his arrest to TMZ in 2012.

In addition, there are perhaps more details than ever before about his standoff with a SWAT team outside his house in 2014 – which he live tweeted throughout while he was barricaded inside his house. Officers were there to serve a warrant for arrest for domestic violence and stalking.

Although Miller has more than a dozen arrests, the episode steers clear of the majority of incidents that involved violence or legal offenses against women, other than the incident with his sister, which Miller plays off in the episode as old-school horseplay like they used to do as kids.

There is, of course, a redemption arc in the episode. A cleaned-up Miller talks in the episode about the journey from his decade-plus of negative headlines to a new version of "Mayhem" now – one who works at Xtreme Couture in a mentorship and coaching role and who is devoted step-dad.

The seven-episode season of the show premieres Sept. 1 at 9 p.m. ET on VICE TV.

Of particular interest to many later in the season will be an episode featuring longtime fighter Phil Baroni, who remains in prison in Mexico on a charge of murder. A teaser video for the season shows a clip of a phone interview with Baroni and him saying his lawyers won't be happy he did the interview. Plus, UFC Hall of Famer Don Frye, "whose willingness to absorb brutality in the cage led to the fight of his life against pain and addiction," is featured in an episode.

Other episodes will feature the marble-mouthed imbecile Tito Ortiz, Chael Sonnen and Mark Coleman. Additionally, the season "will shed new light on one of the most heated feuds in UFC history: Conor McGregor vs. Khabib Nurmagomedov." The seven-episode season will close with a show about the rise and fall of the Affliction clothing brand, which launched a promotion to compete with the UFC, but found itself calling it quits after two events, and a third that was canceled.

Check out the season's official trailer above, and don't miss the premiere episode Tuesday.
